items.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997
items.q: an individualist and an innovator like Miles Davis

ctx.x: I says, “When is he going to breathe?” You’ve got to write — I says, “You wouldn’t write that if you were playing it on your flute or your piccolo or your tenor. You realize I have to take the horn out of my mouth and breathe?” That’s the trap.

I think the space in music is just as important as the notes. You know you get a person like, an individualist and an innovator like Miles Davis, I mean he played one note and the beat’s going on, and he waited, and made you hear a bunch of other notes.
You would lean forward waiting for the next — trying to guess where he was going to put it.
